requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: In contractless mode, `CreateContractlessMembers` selects every public read-write member and never looks at member attributes. A type with no `[MessagePackObject]` or `[DataContract]` therefore still has members marked `[IgnoreMember]` serialized. The same is true for `[IgnoreDataMember]`, which a zero-dependency Project A can use because it is in the BCL. This breaks the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured. The existing contractless resolver skips such members, so a member the type author excluded (for example a secret) is written to the wire.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.cs::ContractlessMode_HonoursIgnoreMember. It drives CSharpGeneratorDriver over a contractless MyObject that has `[IgnoreMember] public int SecretValue`, then asserts the generated formatter does not reference SecretValue. On head it does.

findings.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter's own declaration. A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class F` nested inside a NON-partial containing class passes every check, and no diagnostic is reported. The emitted code (via EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces and the qualified formatter name) then either redeclares the container as partial, which gives CS0260, or emits F outside it, which gives CS0535 on the user's class. Either way the user gets a raw compiler error instead of MsgPack019.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.cs::NestedFormatterInNonPartialContainer_ReportsDiagnosticOrCompiles. It asserts that either the generator reports an error diagnostic or the post-generation compilation has no errors. On head neither holds.

hunches.claim: The docs describe a `SurrogateType` option that this change does not implement. doc/analyzers/MsgPack022.md and the README analyzer index show `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(...))]` and title MsgPack022 "Surrogate member does not match the formatted type". But `GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute` has no members, and the MsgPack022 descriptor and AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md use the title "Serialized member must be public and read-write". A user who follows the documented example gets a compile error.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(S))] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;` against head-built MessagePack.Annotations. Expect CS0246 or CS0117 for `SurrogateType`, which proves the documented example cannot compile. Separately, diff the MsgPack022 title in doc/analyzers/index.md against `SerializedMemberNotSupported.title`.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode serializes only public read-write members, and a class needs an accessible parameterless constructor (otherwise NoDeserializingConstructor is reported). MessagePack's contractless behaviour also covers public get-only members, with deserialization through a matching constructor. So an immutable Project A type with `public int X { get; }` and a constructor is rejected. A type that also has a parameterless constructor silently loses its get-only members, and can serialize as an empty map.

receipt_plan.detail: Take a type `public class P { public P() {} public int X { get; } = 5; public int Y { get; set; } }` with no attributes. Serialize it with ContractlessStandardResolver and with the head-generated `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` formatter, then compare bytes: the generated formatter omits X. Also run the generator on a class that has only `P(int x)` and observe the NoDeserializingConstructor diagnostic.

hunches.claim: Contractless mode ignores `[IgnoreMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]`. `CreateContractlessMembers` takes every public read-write member without checking ignore attributes, so a member that T explicitly marks as ignored is still serialized. This breaks the criterion "If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured".

receipt_plan.detail: Define a Project A type without `[DataContract]` that has `[IgnoreDataMember] public string Secret { get; set; }` plus `public int Id { get; set; }`. Run the generator for a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` class and assert the generated formatter text does not contain `Secret`. It fails on head.

hunches.claim: `[MessagePackFormatter]` attributes on T's members (and on T itself) are not honoured. `CreateMember` always sets `CustomFormatter: null`, so a member with a custom formatter is written with the default resolver formatter. Its bytes then differ from the dynamic or attributed behaviour the criterion "If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured" requires.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a `[MessagePackObject]` type with `[Key(0)][MessagePackFormatter(typeof(MyIntFormatter))] public int A { get; set; }`. Serialize it with DynamicObjectResolver and with the head-generated `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` formatter, then compare bytes. They differ because the custom formatter is ignored.

hunches.claim: Contractless output uses members sorted ordinally by name and string keys. For a [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract] type without keyAsPropertyName, the output uses int or string keys per attribute, but the members' declaring type is set to null. With [DataContract] and Order, int keys may be sparse, but intKey is passed through as the array index. Other generated formatters handle gaps by writing nil for missing indices. It is unclear whether the template does the same for these members, so array layout or deserialization may differ from the dynamic resolver's bytes for the same type.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a [MessagePackObject] class with [Key(0)] and [Key(2)] public properties. Serialize with the dynamic/standard resolver and with the new generated formatter, then compare the bytes (expect nil at index 1 in both).

hunches.claim: Contractless mode here serializes only public read-write members, sorted by ordinal name. The existing ContractlessStandardResolver includes read-only properties and orders members differently (by name too, but via its own rules and includes public readonly fields/get-only props). The wire bytes of the generated formatter for the same type can differ from ContractlessStandardResolver, so users who switch from dynamic contractless to this generated formatter see changed data (missing read-only members).

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a type with public get/set property A, a public get-only property B, and a public readonly field C using ContractlessStandardResolver and the new generated formatter; compare the maps' keys and bytes.

hunches.claim: Test coverage for the new diagnostics is incomplete. There are no tests for MsgPack022, the no-parameterless-constructor path, or the mixed key kinds path. No generator snapshot tests exist for the new template output.

receipt_plan.detail: Mutate the IsPublicReadWrite check in CreateAttributedMembers or the key-kind check and run the tests; expect them to survive.

hunches.claim: Diagnostic MsgPack022 (SerializedMemberNotSupported) and the attributed-mode diagnostics (MemberNeedsKey, BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull, DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys, KeysMustBeUnique, NoDeserializingConstructor) have no test. The only diagnostic tests cover MsgPack019, 020 and 021. Deleting the `!IsPublicReadWrite(member)` guard in CreateAttributedMembers would go unnoticed.

hunches.claim: The [MessagePackObject] attributed path (Key int/string, IgnoreMember, keyAsPropertyName) is untested end to end. The only attributed execution test uses [DataContract] with Order. Mutating the keyAsPropertyName computation, the IgnoreAttribute skip, or the Key handling would not fail any test. The requirement says attributes are honoured when present.

hunches.claim: The tests never cover DataContract with Name-only DataMember (string keys), a mix of string and int keys, or a duplicate key. The DataContract test checks only the array header and a round trip, so a wrong key mapping would still pass. Contractless member ordering (OrderBy Name) is not asserted either.

hunches.claim: The test for registration in the generated resolver asserts only the formatter types. The change to the hand-written formatter exclusion in GeneratorUtilities (the !GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute guard) is not covered by a test that would fail without it. A double registration might produce duplicate resolver entries or a compile error, but only at build time, and no snapshot or generator test covers it.

hunches.claim: No snapshot or generator test checks the emitted source of the partial class. The three diagnostic tests use only hand-written members. The positive generation path (partial class emission, with the StringKey and int-key templates) is verified only by ExecutionTests, which are excluded from MapModeExecutionTests. Mutating the template ternary to always emit 'internal sealed class' would be caught only by a compile error.

hunches.claim: Missing negative cases: no test for a formatted type that is generic, inaccessible, or lacks an accessible parameterless constructor (a class with only a parameterized ctor). hunches.claim: The model built for a user-declared formatter is added to `modelPerType` with no check for whether T is also collected by the TypeCollector. Example: T is in the same compilation and carries `[MessagePackObject]`. Then the resolver gets two ObjectInfos for the same DataType, the auto-generated `internal sealed` formatter and the user's partial one. This causes duplicate registration or hint-name collisions, or the sorted-set merge silently drops one of them, which leaves the user's partial class unimplemented.

Confirm with a generator test where a `[MessagePackObject]` T and a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` formatter for that T coexist, plus a `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver]`, and check for CS8785/CS0535 or a duplicate resolver case.

hunches.claim: The generated-formatter path (GeneratedFormatterCollector) ignores the type's [MessagePackObject]-level security-relevant shape: there is no recursion or depth guard in the generated formatter beyond existing templates, and the collector builds ObjectSerializationInfo with empty constructorParameters for classes. Contractless members of the referenced type are all deserialized through the resolver, so MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth (via the existing template's options.Security.DepthStep) still applies. No new bypass was found, but the collector's GetInstanceMembers walks base types without cycle or depth limits on compile-time data; this is a compile-time concern only, so I am not reporting it as a security issue.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Per L11, types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed, and the TypeCollector does not generate formatters for them. This change adds an explicit opt-in path via the attribute that bypasses this, which fits the requirement and does not contradict the ledger.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] Metadata-only types get no formatter unless the user opts in via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]; the opt-in is deliberate and distinct from the TypeCollector's default behaviour.

narrative: This run reviews reading B of REQ-2129 on branch review/ju26-issue-2129/B: Honour attributes on T when present: if T has [MessagePackObject] or [DataContract], read [Key], [IgnoreMember] and [DataMember] from T via the normal TypeCollector path and fall back to contractless only when T has no attributes. A surrogate type is not required, so the minimal edit is to remove SurrogateType and branch on T's attributes in the collector. As built on the branch: Generated formatters honour [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract] member attributes on the formatted type and fall back to contractless mode only when it has neither; SurrogateType is removed.
